newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN REMAIN WITH PACEMAKERS AFTER WIN OVER HAMBURG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN REMAIN WITH PACEMAKERS AFTER WIN OVER HAMBURG.

text.p: Goals by Alexander Zickler and Christian Nerlinger gave Bayern Munich a somewhat fortunate 2-1 home win over old rivals Hamburg on Saturday, keeping Giovanni Trapattoni's side in third place in the Bundesliga.
Zickler opened the scoring for the 13-times champions in the seventh minute.
Harald Spoerl hit back for Hamburg early in the second half but a spectacular long-range shot from Nerlinger in the 63rd minute secured both points for Bayern.

Holding on to their third slot was the best Bayern could do on Saturday as wins for leaders VfB Stuttgart and second-placed Bayer Leverkusen on Friday night ensured there would be no change at the top.
"The result was really important for us but we were lucky to win," Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni acknowledged after the game. "Hamburg deserved at least a draw."
The former Internazionale boss said Bayern's performance did not match their display in the 2-1 win over Borussia Moenchengladbach in the second round of the cup on Wednesday.
South African striker Sean Dundee, the Bundesliga's leading scorer, collected his ninth goal of the season in Karlsruhe's 1-0 away win over Schalke, moving them up to fourth place.

The home side got a frosty reception from their own fans for the sacking of coach Joerg Berger during the week. Some key players, unhappy about Berger's training methods and leadership style, had requested his dismissal.
"Our nerves were totally finished after such a turbulent week," said caretaker coach Herbert Neu. "And then we had to deal with the whistles and chants of the fans as well."
Cologne, beginning the day in fourth spot, slipped to sixth with a 3-0 defeat at promoted Duisburg.
"It was a very one-sided game," admitted Cologne coach Peter Neururer. "Duisburg were physically and mentally fired up, we just stood there."
Stuttgart's Brazilian striker Giovane Elber was the key figure in their 4-2 win over Freiburg.
The early-season pacesetters were reduced to 10 men in the 29th minute when Dutch libero Frank Verlaat was sent off for a challenge on compatriot Harry Decheiver.
But Stuttgart, inspired by the return of playmaker Krassimir Balakov after injury, refused to be discouraged. Thomas Schneider put them 2-1 ahead in the 39th minute. Decheiver equalised in the 52nd.
Balakov set up Elber's first in the 64th minute and he added a second four minutes later to secure the points.
The leaders' form was in marked contrast to that of champions Borussia Dortmund who went down 1-0 to promoted Bochum on Friday. They lie six points off the lead in fifth place.
Ravaged by injury, Dortmund never got into gear and a goal by defender Thomasz Waldoch was enough to give Bochum a famous win over their wealthy local rivals.
